bytes.c copies a into unsigned char[4] (object representation, 6.2.6.1p4) and prints 42 00 00 00 from index 0; byte order is implementation-defined (6.2.6.1p2) and the claim scopes it to this machine, which is little-endian.

Mechanism: '(double)a is a new object' is false; a cast yields a value, not an object. In bytes.c the bytes belong to the object d that the value is stored in (line 6). Also the 8-byte size and byte order are platform facts with no 'on this machine' scope.
